summary: Independent review of task 26.3 (Guard enforcement) after the attempt-2 rework. I inspected the full diff of scripts/check-agents.sh, docs/agent-contracts.md and docs/plan/README.md; confirmed no pre-existing check was weakened and that all 13 pre-existing sections survive with their logic intact; and reproduced every probe myself on a throwaway copy at /tmp/26.3/repo (now removed). TQ-01 is genuinely closed: the pre-change all-phases reviewer-report listing rule is restored as its own ungated section ('plan state lists the reviewer report from every phase', scripts/check-agents.sh:141-170) whose logic is byte-identical to the HEAD section modulo the comment and the end label; de-listing task 15.1 fails with the byte-identical pre-change line under both the new script and git-show HEAD:scripts/check-agents.sh, and the from-phase-20 on-disk evidence section independently still reports ok on that mutation, so the two sections neither shadow nor weaken each other. TQ-02 is closed: role_mix is now the reduce over the union of task-record invocations and the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries, so it sums to subagent_invocations_total; with AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE lowered to 20 I measured phase 20 reconciling on every field including role_mix {worker 4, reviewer 4, tqr 3, phase-reviewer 2} and phase 21 reconciling, run exit 0; and I recomputed the phase-21 aggregate independently from the fourteen task records (56 invocations, cost 1.403849754, tokens 293509314, duration 46658s, rework 7, review rounds 20, test-quality rounds 6, role mix 19/20/6/4/5/2) matching the amended record exactly. Scope is exactly the three permitted files plus the 26.3 report directory; no product code, tests, artifacts, manifest, docs/plan/state.json, PLANS.md, docs/status.md, docs/changelog/, docs/limitations/ or other docs/implementation/** record changed, and no commit or tag was created. findings.summary: The TQ-03 check enforces presence and equality but not completeness of the phase-reviewer set, and it is skipped entirely when a phase-review*.json exists with no orchestration record.
findings.detail: Measured boundaries of the new check, in the interest of an honest record rather than as a required change. (1) Two phase-review files on disk (phase-review.json plus phase-review.attempt-2.json) with only one phase-reviewer entry still passes: the glob sets a boolean, not a count, so the check cannot express 'one invocation per review file'. (2) A phase >= 26 directory containing phase-review.json but no orchestration.json passes completely - the aggregate section's [ -f "$o" ] || continue skips it, and no other section requires a phase record to exist. (3) Conversely a phase-26 record carrying a phase-reviewer entry while no phase-review*.json exists also passes; that is the documented release-review-as-gate shape and is correct. (4) The glob is broad enough to match both the base and attempt filenames, which is what makes the phase-20 two-attempt precedent work. These are all completeness limits, not soundness limits: no probe can make the guard detect an invocation set that the phase record itself under-reports, because the record is the only authority for its own invocations. The worker discloses exactly this in known_limitations[2] ('the guard enforces presence, equality and per-entry sums, not completeness of the set'), so it is disclosed rather than hidden, and the residual direction is a false pass over an under-reported phase-reviewer set, which the phase review and the gate are the authorities for. Not blocking: the required conditions are enforced and the contract wording no longer overstates them.

findings.summary: The phase record's own subagents entries of non-phase-reviewer roles are outside the aggregate recomputation, so the union basis is a definition rather than a whole-array read.
findings.detail: The guard derives the phase-reviewer contribution from the phase record's own subagents array but takes every other role from the task records, then unions them. A consequence I measured: adding an extra non-phase-reviewer entry (a security-reviewer) to the phase record's own subagents while leaving the aggregate untouched still PASSES, whereas recording that same entry and including it in the aggregate correctly FAILS. In other words the guard's contract is 'the phase record's own array carries the task-record invocations plus any phase-reviewer entries' (as the guard comment states) - it is not 'every entry in the phase record's array is authoritative'. Both in-repo records honour that shape: phase 20's own 13-entry array is exactly the 11 task-level invocations plus its 2 phase-reviewer entries, and phase 21's own 56-entry array is exactly its 56 task-level invocations. So the definition matches the project's own convention, and the delegation for this task specified precisely this union ('task-level plus the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries'). The worker discloses the underlying limitation in interpretations[0].impact ('a phase record whose copied task-level entries diverge from the task records is not detected by role_mix'). Worth recording because a future phase that dispatches a genuinely phase-level non-phase-reviewer role (a phase-level documentation-maintainer producing phase-<n>/documentation-update.json, as phases 9-12 do) would hit a confusing failure. Not blocking and not required: changing the recomputation to a whole-array read would break the phase-20 and phase-21 records, which are immutable history.
